messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]     MRN: [REDACTED]     DOB: [REDACTED]     Admission Date: [REDACTED]     Discharge Date: [REDACTED]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of chest pain, shortness of breath, and a productive cough. Upon examination, the patient was found to have tachycardia and tachypnea. Laboratory findings revealed leukocytosis with elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate. CT chest showed left lower lobe pneumonia and a large pericardial effusion. The patient received appropriate treatment for pneumonia and underwent transthoracic echocardiogram to further characterize the effusion as moderate circumferential pericardial effusion.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Upon consultation with the patient’s psychiatrist, clozapine was stopped, which was thought to be the cause for the non-resolving pericardial effusion. Following the discontinuation of the drug, there was a gradual improvement in the respiratory status. The patient was discontinued from clozapine and discharged to home in stable and improved condition.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient is advised to follow up with their primary care provider for future management of high cholesterol and assistance with smoking cessation.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
None prescribed at this time.

FOLLOW-UP STUDIES:
Transthoracic echocardiogram to be repeated for further evaluation in one year.

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
Stable and improved.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The key coding question is what the principal diagnosis is. The patient has left lower lobe pneumonia and a large pericardial effusion that was attributed to clozapine and did not resolve. The effusion was the focus of the workup (echocardiogram) and of the drug cessation.

The candidate categories are:
- **Pneumonia:** J18 (unspecified organism).
- **Pericardial effusion:** I31 (other diseases of pericardium, which includes pericardial effusion, non-inflammatory). Drug-induced effusion would be coded I31.3 with an adverse-effect code, Y49.x.
- **Pericarditis:** I30. This is possible, given the elevated CRP and ESR, but the summary describes an effusion rather than pericarditis.

The discharge diagnosis section is withheld, so the principal diagnosis has to be inferred from the rest of the summary. The case appears to come from a report of clozapine-induced pericardial effusion, and the pneumonia was treated appropriately. The stated reason for the non-resolving course was the effusion, and the main management change was stopping clozapine. The condition chiefly responsible for the workup and the drug change is the pericardial effusion, so I chose I31.

**I31**
